gap: No result ChatGPT got works out, for each candidate, how many watts are left for a third device (a phone) while both laptops keep 100 W. The answer is 0 W on the Anker Prime 200W (A2683), the Satechi 200W 6-port and the UGREEN Nexode 200W 6-port. It is 40 W on the Satechi ChargeView 240W (C1+C2+C3 = 100+100+40). The Anker Prime 250W has at most 50 W left by its stated totals, but Anker publishes no per-port split for it.
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages: anker.com A2683 and A2345, the Satechi 200W manual, the Satechi ChargeView power-distribution FAQ, Macworld's Anker Prime 250W review and computingforgeeks' 'Real Port Splits' guide. computingforgeeks gives the A2683 '100W + 100W' but says nothing about a third device. The A2683 page gives only port-count totals (200 W with 3 ports), so the 0 W figure is implied, not stated. Macworld's 250W review gives no measured splits. ChatGPT's answers only hedged that a third device 'may reduce' power. Satechi's own ChargeView FAQ states 100+100+40 for that one charger, and that is why this scores 2 and not 3. No page lines the candidates up side by side.
decides: If the shopper only ever plugs in two laptops, this confirms ChatGPT's pick, the Anker Prime 200W at $69.99 ($35.00 per 100 W laptop slot). If a phone also has to charge while both laptops stay at 100 W, every 200 W candidate drops out, because 200 − 200 = 0 W. The pick then moves to the Satechi ChargeView 240W ($149.99, 40 W documented for C3) or the Anker Prime 250W (up to 50 W by its totals, but no published split).
